searchText: lol for starters maybe discuss why ossification after PoS is not acceptable? The main things that I think people really want post-PoS are: * Data sharding * Statelessness + state expiry * ZK-SNARKing the EVM and other state transitions * Miscellaneous security upgrades like VDF oracle, proof of custody, etc Account abstraction (can be done mostly-off-chain with flashbots-like techniques, so it doesn't strictly require consensus changes (!!). And the cost of those changes above being delayed is definitely significantly lower than the cost of the merge being delayed. There is value in *eventually* calcifying the protocol as that gives people long-term confidence in the system (changes bring risk with them). However, I think this industry is still in its infancy and has a long way to go before it is to the point where calcification makes sense. From past experience I would argue that the notion of "this software is finished, we won't ever need to change it again" is often a bad decision. So in my opinion the cost of scheduling something like yearly update slots via an ice age is definitely lower than the risk of premature stagnation. Note that those hardforks can also be of the type "Everything running smoothly here, we'll just push back the ice age". idk... Ice age is basically consensus today deciding and acting to bind consensus in the future. idk if we have, as @ Micah says, a clear enough plan for the future, to want to bind ourselves to it. So if social consensus changes tomorrow and says they dont want zksnarks built into layer one or whatever, why cant future us have the freedom to choose that? instead of deciding today itself that future us must implement zksnarks on L1 .. and it should be more effort to decide not to do it We can. The point of having the protocol "require" regular maintenance is just to help force routine coordination points. It prevents calcification via filibustering (at the extreme). implying routine coordination points are a good thing? (at current stage of ethereum) Yes, because they can prevent some pathological human coordination problems. Defaults are powerful, and if the default is "do nothing" then it requires a lot more "effort" to do *something*/*anything*. By making the default "do something", then getting a change (any change) pushed through no longer requires overcoming the power of the default. Yes, I see it like putting scheduled election intervals into the constitution. Nobody forces you to de-elect a good government, but if something needs to change you are glad for the scheduled election. If one *desires* no-change, then a default of no-change is a good idea. If one *desires* change, then a default of change is a good idea. And it's definitely possible to have social contracts in favor of ossification of *some* parts of the protocol but not others here, by effort you mean ability to get social consensus, right? rather than writing code etc Yeah, it is definitely the humans that are the problem. 🙂 so we should have ice ages on some part of the protocol? 🙂 (more specifically is there any part of ethereum that is mature enough to calcify .. atleast calcify enough for a default inclination towards doing nothing to be better and changing it to require work) It is quite difficult do a partial upgrade cadence with the current architecture, and there aren't any "pieces" big enough to extract out that are "ready to calcify" to be worth it I don't think. cool thanks So are there any further ideas on how to actually build a PoS ice age? Delaying slots looks easy at first sight, but I'm not sure about what stuff implicitly depends on regular slots. And the regular slots are a bit too beautiful to touch them tbh 🙂 Invalidating slots might work, but I'm not sure if there is non-gameable randomness around to do so, so that it isn't gameable by the other validators / block proposers. But then it doesn't even have to be random. Something like "slot x mod n is invalid", where n is very large initially and then slowly decreasing could work. Simplest solution is to just increase block time. A more hard-line approach is to just stop block production. I think gradually stopping block production is preferable to a hard stop. Maybe just the first block of every epoch, then the first two, and so on I may not be good about following rules but in general I am good at knowing them. And governance issues are explicitly not allowed in this server, so I'll stick to the technical part on how to implement an ICE age. I think PoS allows for a few more variants that weren't there in PoW. Randomly declaring more and more blocks invalid could be very complicated to implement cause you'll have to reinclude transactions and the execution and consensus layers are weakly coupled after the merge. I think changing block time is really hard to implement for clients since clock sync is one of the foundations of the networking stack of PsS. One thing that can be done is to require more and more consecutive justified epochs to declare one to be finalized. This way you can delay finalization without really changing execution at all. Then parties will have to either go back and resort to number of blocks to confirm transactions (knowing that is cheaper in PoS for some players to actually have long chains without them being finalized) or pressure devs to get back to work Another thing that can be done is reduce the number of attestations that are included per block Screwing randomly some stakers. And also preventing finalization slowly

* Statelessness + state expiry
* ZK-SNARKing the EVM and other state transitions

Account abstraction (can be done mostly-off-chain with flashbots-like techniques, so it doesn't strictly require consensus changes (!!). And the cost of those changes above being delayed is definitely significantly lower than the cost of the merge being delayed.
